fingerprint.fps: variable, 30 nominal; 22095 video frames in 1102.77 s

interventions.what: Bandicam window capture of the Isle Wars Pro game window; the owner played one game from the options screen to the end screen (18:23 recording). The video file is the only output. No scripted clicks. Counters, seats and screens were read from pixels by region comparison and template matching of glyph shapes, with no OCR pass.

start_state.restore: Owner launched a new game on the unregistered Pro build from the options screen (seat 1 human, three computer seats, middle strength). Pro has no save file (C-SET-05), so no state was restored. The recording starts on the title screen; the opening deal is the first board.

args: probe: 1102.77 s, 22095 video frames, variable frame rate (nominal 30), 1920x1080 H.264, AAC 48 kHz stereo, 134194220 bytes
ffmpeg 8.0.1; the panel regions were read frame by frame from the container timestamps; offsets are mm:ss.mmm video offsets
record content: the 76 attacks of the game (32 human, 44 computer) with their start counters, strip states, endings, capture splits and the human move-in counters

observations.field: reading method
observations.value: the two-line counter strip (bottom right, the attacker's armies and the defender's armies) was read at every frame where it changed, by matching glyph shapes of the digits (no OCR); the two country counters on the map were read before and after each attack by matching the large digits at the 46 country anchors; the owner of a country was read from its colour at the anchor (a selection or capture flash changes the colour for about 0.4 s, so counts decide, not colours, right after a capture). A capture is the two country counters adding up to the attacker armies at the capture; the last exchange of a capture is inferred (defender 1 to 0). The same readers as for IP1 027 (E018-r0006), with the digit templates extended to the larger stacks of this game.

observations.field: what the strip shows first
observations.value: as in IP1 027: for the human the strip first shows the counters before any exchange; for the computer the strip appears after its first exchange, so the start is taken from the country counters just before the strip (the before reading).
